hook.line: Tomás has dialled the wrong number twice this week, and both times he only managed an English *sorry*. Here's the line that lets him back out gracefully.
hook.en: Sorry, I got the wrong number.

examples.en: Sorry, I got the wrong number.
I made a mistake with the bill.
They went to the wrong door.

rule:
In English you say *I got the wrong number*. Spanish says you *made a mistake of* number: *me equivoqué de número*.

After *de*, name the thing you picked wrongly. No *el* or *la*: *de número*, *de bus*, *de calle*, *de día*.

The verb is *equivocarse* and always has *me / te / se / nos*: *me equivoqué*, *te equivocaste*, *se equivocó*, *nos equivocamos*.

When you slipped up *inside* something (a bill, a spelling), use *en*: *Me equivoqué en la cuenta*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a pronominal verb (it comes with *me, te, se*) followed by a preposition.

options: Sorry, I got the wrong number.
Sorry, you got the wrong number.
He went to the wrong door.
They went to the wrong door.
I made a mistake with the bill.
You went to the wrong house.
She went to the wrong house.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *en*: Perdón, me equivoqué ___ número. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: Wrong number means the wrong one of something: *de número*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *en*: Me equivoqué ___ la cuenta. Type the whole sentence.
Say: We got the wrong bus.
Say to a friend: You got the wrong day.
Say: Tomás took the wrong street.
Say: They went to the wrong door.
Make it about we: *Me equivoqué de número.*
yourTurn.why: Both the pronoun and the verb change: *nos equivocamos*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. You still need *de* before what you got wrong.
For a mistake inside something, like a bill, it's *en*.

personal: Think of a time you went to the wrong place or the wrong day. Write it with *me equivoqué de...*
